comments.text: I met some people from Uzbekistan in 2001. They were staying at the same hotel as I was at Mount Carmel in the northern city of Haifa in Israel. Over a thousand people from all corners of the world were there for the inauguration of the Baha’i International Teaching Centre. I shared breakfast table with the Uzbek friends and was delighted to learn about their country, people and culture. They were all wonderful and wanted to know about Australia. At first they thought I was from Austria but when I explained where Australia was, they were fascinated. They come from a landlocked country they could not believe that Australia was not only a country but a continent located between the Pacific, the Indian and the Great Southern Oceans. Recently I saw a volunteer position with Australian Volunteers for International Development  in Mongolia for an English teacher and was tempted to apply for it but I do have some serious heath issues and the thoughts of living in a very cold country made me stop.
